observation.visible_scene: A brightly lit dance studio with a full-height mirror wall along the back, framed pictures and hanging lights above it, a low blue-white wall/base beneath the mirror, wooden ballet barres (including a free-standing white barre unit on the right), a small phone lying motionless on the floor, and a woman wearing a black tank top, black flared pants and a sheer light-grey flowing over-top who is dancing. Both the dancer and a mirrored figure of her are visible in the frame.
visible_changes: The dancer's arms move in continuous flowing arcs: starting low at her sides, sweeping out to shoulder height, then rising overhead with the sheer sleeves fluttering, and later lowering again toward the end of the segment.
One leg periodically extends outward to the side (a pointed foot reaching left) while the other supports her, then retracts.

Her torso rotates through the sequence: initially in left profile, then turning so her back faces the camera at the left edge of the frame, while the figure seen in the mirror shows a corresponding front/back orientation and arm positions.

The body shifts horizontally: the foreground figure drifts from center-left toward the left edge and stays pinned near that edge for the latter half, whereas the mirrored figure remains roughly centered in the mirror, executing turns and arm raises in sync with the foreground figure.
The camera and background (pictures, barres, floor seams, phone) remain fixed; all change is the dancer's motion, not camera movement.
The sheer over-top deforms and billows around the arms as they move, indicating light flowing fabric rather than a rigid garment.
outside_clip_unknowns: The start and end of the dance phrase are not shown; motion is already in progress at t=0 and continues past t=2.67s.
What triggers or follows the sequence, and whether the mirrored figure is the same dancer's reflection or a second person, cannot be confirmed from within this crop.
uncertain_details: The horizontal offset between the foreground figure (left) and the figure in the mirror (center) is large and persistent; this could be a reflection under an oblique mirror/camera geometry or a second dancer in identical clothing—orientation alone is mirrored, so the exact identity is not fully resolvable.
Frame-level leg/foot contact points are partly hidden by the low wall base, so precise foot placement is uncertain.
